literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe the same construct from the same paper (PMC10941171): full-length BTN1A1 cloned into the pCDH lentiviral vector with a FLAG tag, used to generate stable cell lines. The construct is membrane-anchored and full-length — it clears the 'soluble ectodomain' exclusion. However, neither clip states the position of the FLAG tag. The prompt rule is explicit: 'a commercial plasmid whose tag POSITION is unstated; you cannot pin insert_after_residue.' The naming convention 'BTN1A1-FLAG' (gene symbol followed by tag) universally denotes a C-terminal fusion. BTN1A1 is a type I single-pass membrane protein: its N-terminus (residues 27–246) is extracellular and its C-terminus (residues 268–526) is intracellular. A C-terminal FLAG would therefore sit on the cytoplasmic face — not an extracellular surface tag. No topology-derived N-terminal site can be inferred from a C-terminal tag name. No other ledger line names any internal extracellular loop insertion, fluorescent-protein fusion, transposon screen, or any other tolerated insertion in the extracellular domain of BTN1A1 or a close ortholog. Result: zero qualifying extracellular surface tag sites.

literature_other_positions.note: The 'BTN1A1-FLAG' naming convention indicates a C-terminal FLAG tag; residue 526 (the C-terminus) falls within the intracellular domain (residues 268–526) of this type I membrane protein, making it a cytoplasmic tag, not an extracellular surface tag.
